Title: IED experts contribute to the newly launched Sindh Education Sector Plan
NewsSummary: Efforts to reform education in Sindh received a boost with the launch of the Sindh Education Sector Plan (SESP) 2014-18 by the provincial government on September 29, 2014.
NewsContent:
Efforts to reform education in Sindh received a boost with the launch of the Sindh Education Sector Plan (SESP) 2014-18 by the provincial government on September 29, 2014. This Rs. 940bn plan aims to educate children aged five to 16 in Sindh and is supported by donors including the European Union, Global Partnership in Education, USAID and the World Bank. The formulation of SESP represents an important policy and planning milestone in the ongoing education reform process in Sindh following the 18th Amendment to the Constitution of the country which devolved the responsibility of providing free and compulsory education to all children aged five to 16 years to the provincial governments. 

Being mindful of the two key deficiencies in the provincial education system - access to educational opportunities and low quality of education- the plan provides the provincial government an opportunity to take systematic steps to ensure equity in access, enhance the quality, improve governance and service delivery, and facilitate equity in resource allocation. Developed on the basis of the fundamental tenets of the National Education Policy and the National Curriculum, SESP is envisioned to contribute towards achieving the National Poverty Reduction Strategy goals, the internationally-agreed Education for All commitments, Millennium Development Goals and, most importantly, the recently passed Sindh Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2013.

The plan has been developed after two years of extensive consultation and engagement of key stakeholders from the public and private education sectors in Sindh. IED played a key role in developing the Plan's vision and strategy with faculty being part of two consultative groups during the two years. Professor Dr Muhammad Memon, as part of the Expert Advisory Group provided input on the long-term policy objectives and strategic direction of the plan, while Dr Sajid Ali, Assistant Professor, was part of the Local Education Group, which worked as a broader consultative body for developing the details of the plan. They were building on IED's experience with the development of the National Education Policy in 2009 and review of the National Curriculum Framework in 2006.
